newsitem.title: UK: Tanker rates steady, demand firms Caribbean trips.
newsitem.headline: Tanker rates steady, demand firms Caribbean trips.

text.p: Tanker charter rates were steady to firmer on Monday with very large crude carriers (VLCCs) to Singapore slightly higher, shipbrokers said.
Rates for cross Med and Caribs-upcoast voyages for smaller tonnage also crept higher, they added.
Focus of trade remained on eastward voyages from the Mideast, but only rates for 250,000 tonners to Singapore were any higher, rising 2.5 wordlscale points to W76.5 in active business.

Rates for voyages for 250,000 tonnes from the Mideast were firm. Rates to the West were assessed around W65 while other Asian voyages for 250,000 tonnes were firm at W75 after rising sharply last week on the back of strong Singapore rates.
Rates to Japan were still estimated up around W85 for 250,000 tonnes although trade for this route has been slower recently.
Brokers said the scarce availability of VLCC tonnage through August, with most vessels already chartered, might push rates a little higher.
But they said the market was looking generally balanced with loading requirements also mostly covered for the month.
However, Iraqi crude oil exports appear imminent, perhaps resuming in a week to 10 days time.
Brokers said this could put further upward pressure on rates as Iraq may need to squeeze out up to two million bpd in order to reach a cash target by an early September deadline.
Exports are to emerge from the port of Ceyhan in Turkey and at the Gulf terminal of Mina al Bakr.
U.S. refiner Bayoil was reported to have fixed the 337,000 tonne Concordia 1 on-subs out of Ceyhan last week.
The increasing tendency for U.S. oil refiners to buy shorter-haul crudes saw rates for 70,000 tonners from the Caribbean and Mexico to the U.S Gulf averaging around W145 in active trade.
Rates elsewhere were little changed. Aframax tankers moving across the Med were talked at around W110 while million-barrel vessels were talked closer to W77.5-80.

Cross-North Sea routes for 80,000 tonners were pegged at around W90-95 while a recent drop in fixings from West African to the U.S. Gulf saw rates off around five worldscale points with 260,000 tonnes taking W162.5 and 130,000 tonnes W75.
